subtopic: Electronic Form 222 copies and CSOS order records
stem: A pharmacy is revising its electronic records for Schedule I and II procurement. The system contains electronic copies of DEA Forms 222 as well as orders executed through the Controlled Substance Ordering System (CSOS). Which conclusions are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A paper Form 222 may be filed with all other pharmacy records as long as staff can locate it with a keyword search.
An electronic copy of a Form 222 may be stored with other records if it is readily retrievable separately from those records.
A digitally signed CSOS order is an alternative ordering record, not merely an electronic copy of a Form 222.
Scanning a completed paper Form 222 converts it into a CSOS order.
The rule governing preservation of CSOS electronic orders is distinct from the rule governing storage of electronic Form 222 copies.

explanation.core_reasoning: The records must first be classified correctly. An electronic copy of a Form 222 is deemed maintained separately when it can be readily retrieved separately, even if it shares an electronic system with other records. A compliant, digitally signed CSOS order is a different authorized ordering record and is preserved under the electronic-order provisions. Merely scanning a paper Form 222 does not transform it into a CSOS order, and the separate-filing rule for paper Forms 222 is not replaced by ordinary keyword searchability.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect: paper Forms 222 are subject to the separate-maintenance requirement; the electronic-copy retrieval rule does not erase that distinction.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: ready separate retrievability satisfies the separate-maintenance condition for an electronic Form 222 copy.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: a compliant CSOS order is its own digitally signed electronic ordering instrument, used as an alternative to Form 222.
choice_analysis.D: A scan is an electronic copy of the paper form, not a digitally signed CSOS order.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: CSOS order preservation and electronic Form 222 copy storage are addressed by different provisions.

related_facts: Form 222 records and compliant electronic orders must be retained for the applicable federal retention period
Electronic-order records kept on a central server must remain readily retrievable at the registered location
explanation.mpje_trap: Both records may appear on a computer screen, but an electronic copy of Form 222 and a digitally signed CSOS order are legally different record objects.

reasoning_steps: Classify each record as a paper Form 222, an electronic Form 222 copy, or a CSOS order
Apply separate-maintenance rules according to the record type
Test whether an electronic copy is readily retrievable separately
Keep the CSOS ordering and preservation framework distinct from Form 222 copy storage
